statement: For every positive integer n and every subset D of the proper positive divisors of n, let ICG_n(D) be the simple graph on Z_n in which distinct x,y are adjacent exactly when gcd(x-y,n) lies in D. Among graphs that are uniquely 3-colorable and have clique number 2, the least possible order is n=60. At that least order the complete classification by equality of labeled graphs is the single divisor set D={2,5}; its unique unordered color-class partition consists of the three residue classes modulo 3.
contribution: An exact exhaustive census of all 4,091 legal pairs through order 60 sharpens the previously known order-60 construction to the least order in the frozen (chi,omega)=(3,2) scope and classifies every divisor set at that order. A separately implemented neighbor-set/union-find/CNF-DPLL verifier reproduces every classification and checks every primary certificate. This does not claim unrestricted minimality for uniquely k-colorable integral circulants with arbitrary k>omega, and the bounded source comparison is not a claim of priority.
